annotation.title_clean: Working paper by Japan on emerging technologies in the area of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (CCW/GGE.1/2024/WP.8)
annotation.title_en: Working paper by Japan on emerging technologies in the area of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (CCW/GGE.1/2024/WP.8)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Government of Japan (submission to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS
annotation.summary_en: Japan's July 2024 working paper to the CCW GGE on lethal autonomous weapons. It stresses IHL applicability, human-centric control within a responsible chain of command, accountability, risk mitigation and legal weapons reviews, and favours effective, consensus-based rules (not necessarily legally binding) over technology-specific bans.
key_provisions_or_claims: IHL applies to all weapons; systems incapable of IHL compliance must not be used.
Fully autonomous lethal systems operating without human involvement should not be permitted.
Weapon systems must operate within a responsible chain of human command and control with attributable responsibility.
Risk assessment, bias minimisation, testing, and Article 36 legal reviews should be applied and good practices shared.
Outcome should be effective rules by consensus, not necessarily legally binding; LAWS talks separate from responsible military AI.
